hook: Creatine is the most researched supplement in sports nutrition, and it still gets sold like a shortcut.

Creatine is the most researched supplement in sports nutrition, and it still gets sold like a shortcut.

Without training, lean mass gains were not significant — creatine alone did nothing for muscle.

title: Are you making one of these 4 critical mistakes? 📉
hook: Are you making one of these 4 critical mistakes? 📉
caption:
Are you making one of these 4 critical mistakes? 📉

You can train 6 days a week and eat perfectly, but if you are doing these 4 things in the gym, you are leaving massive gains on the table.

1️⃣ Ego Lifting: Leave your pride at the door. Form > Weight. 2️⃣ Routine Hopping: "Muscle confusion" is a myth. Stick to a routine for 8 weeks and apply progressive overload. 3️⃣ Team No Sleep: You break muscle down in the gym. You build it in bed. 4️⃣ Rushing: The eccentric (lowering) phase causes the most growth. Slow down! 🐌

Be honest, which one of these are you guilty of? 👇

title: Frequency organizes the work. It does not create the work.
hook: Frequency organizes the work. It does not create the work.
caption:
Frequency organizes the work. It does not create the work.

Training a muscle more often changes how weekly work is distributed. In a 2019 meta-analysis of 25 studies, higher and lower frequencies produced similar average hypertrophy when weekly volume was equated.

A newer dose-response meta-regression was compatible with a negligible independent effect of volume-adjusted frequency on hypertrophy. This does not mean every schedule is identical. Frequency can change session length, sets per session, days in the gym, and how manageable the plan feels. Strength may also respond differently.

When you’re bulking, you can’t let the scale discourage you. 💪🏽

Some days you’ll feel lean, other days you’ll feel a little fuller — but that doesn’t mean you’re going backwards. Trust the training. Trust the nutrition. Trust the process.

I’m not chasing a smaller number on the scale. I’m chasing stronger legs, fuller muscles, better performance, and progress. 🔥

Eat. Train. Recover. GROW.

title: The programme looks advanced because fatigue is high.
hook: The programme looks advanced because fatigue is high.
caption:
The programme looks advanced because fatigue is high.

That is an easy mistake to make.

More exercises.
More sets.
More intensity techniques.
More changes from one week to the next.

It can all look sophisticated on paper.

But the real test is whether the work can be recovered from and repeated.

When fatigue rises faster than recovery can keep up, performance starts to flatten. Technique becomes less reliable. Sessions that once felt productive begin to feel heavy for no clear reason.
